title: Does label benefit depend on stimulus difficulty and AI familiarity?
rationale: Automated Flagging raised accuracy by 4.4 points (p=0.004) in the source study, but the familiarity heterogeneity table (E2) was empty and some high-familiarity arm halves had n=38 or fewer. This follow-up tests whether the gain holds across easy vs hard stimuli and across prior AI familiarity, with enough power for an interaction test.
contribution: Tests whether the automated-label gain is conditional on stimulus difficulty and prior AI familiarity, using a preregistered moderator and an adequately powered sample.
limitations: Interaction tests need several hundred respondents per cell, so the interaction may remain underpowered.
Oversampling high-familiarity respondents may limit generalisation to the whole population.
Generator age is only a proxy for difficulty.

design.title: Automated labels by stimulus difficulty and AI familiarity
design.overview: Respondents first report AI familiarity (ai_scale), with high-familiarity respondents oversampled. They are then randomised to a control or an automated AI-detection label. Each respondent judges 8 posts (images and text) in a within-person mix of older-generator (easy) and recent-generator (hard) AI outputs and authentic items. The outcome is d' and its interaction with difficulty and with familiarity.
design.hypothesis: H1: automated labels raise d' relative to control (0.035 minimum effect). H2: the label gain is smaller for hard (recent-generator) stimuli. H3: the label gain differs by ai_scale (high vs low familiarity).
design.primaryOutcome: Discernment d' (z(hit rate) minus z(false-alarm rate)) across the 8 posts, with condition by difficulty and condition by ai_scale interaction tests.
design.comparison: Control vs automated label, crossed within person with stimulus difficulty (older vs recent generator), and moderated by ai_scale (pre-treatment).
design.population: US online panel adults, with high AI-familiarity respondents oversampled.

assumptions: Power target: about 500 per arm to detect 0.035 at 80% power (source H1 Automated Flagging effect 0.044); a halved interaction would need several hundred per cell, so total N is about 1,000, with high-familiarity respondents oversampled via panel quotas.
ai_scale is measured pre-treatment, with a median split and continuous analysis both preregistered.

Only two example posts per arm are shown in the flow; the full 8-post feed (4 older-generator, 4 recent-generator; image and text; half authentic) follows the same pattern with randomised order and fixed label accuracy.
d' is computed per respondent with a log-linear correction; a multiplicity plan (Holm across H1-H3) is preregistered.
Platform: online US panel, about 10 minutes.
unresolved: The actual image and text stimuli, including older vs recent generator outputs, must be supplied by the research team.
The automated label accuracy rate and wording must be fixed by the research team.
Compensation and IRB approval number must be supplied by the research team.
